what_its_for: Tezepelumab-ekko is used to help control moderate-to-severe asthma in adults and children 12 years and older. It works by blocking a protein in your body that triggers swelling and tightening in your airways. This medicine helps reduce asthma attacks and may help you breathe better over time. It is NOT a rescue inhaler and will NOT stop a sudden asthma attack.
how_to_take: Tezepelumab-ekko is given as a shot (injection) under your skin, usually in your stomach, thigh, or upper arm. A healthcare provider will give you this injection in a clinic or doctor's office. It comes as a prefilled autoinjector pen or a prefilled syringe. Your doctor or nurse will show you or your caregiver how to give the injection at home if that is appropriate for you. Always rotate injection sites and never inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or hard. Continue using all your other asthma medicines unless your doctor tells you to stop.
dosing: The usual dose is 210 mg given as one injection every 4 weeks (once a month). Your doctor will determine the exact schedule that is right for you. Do not change your dose or how often you take it without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give the injection as soon as you remember. Then continue on your regular monthly schedule from that date. Do not give two injections at the same time to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store tezepelumab-ekko in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for a maximum of 30 days, but once removed from the refrigerator, do not put it back. Discard it if not used within 30 days at room temperature. Keep all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not use tezepelumab-ekko to treat a sudden asthma attack or breathing emergency — always use your quick-relief rescue inhaler for that. Do not stop taking your other asthma medicines (such as inhaled steroids) unless your doctor tells you to, even if you start feeling better. Avoid injecting into skin that is damaged, scarred, or affected by skin conditions. Tell your doctor about all vaccines before getting one, as live vaccines are generally not recommended while using this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: sudden shortness of breath or a serious asthma attack, signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, dizziness, fast heartbeat, or trouble breathing), fever, joint pain, or rash after injection (possible signs of serum sickness-like reaction), signs of a parasitic (worm) infection such as stomach pain, nausea, or changes in bowel habits, any new or worsening symptoms that concern you. Also call your doctor if your asthma does not improve after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Tezepelumab-ekko is a long-term treatment that works gradually over time. Most people start to notice fewer asthma attacks and improved breathing within a few weeks to a few months of starting treatment. It is important to keep taking it regularly even if you do not notice immediate results. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Tezepelumab-ekko is approved for children 12 years and older at the same adult dose. It has not been studied in children under 12. Pregnancy: It is not known if tezepelumab-ekko is safe during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Older adults: No dose adjustment is generally needed for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustments are currently recommended, but always tell your doctor about any medical conditions you have.
